residual.title: Per exercise, mergeActual keeps one whole entry, so a known load is replaced by an unknown one when the other entry has as many known values
residual.mechanism: mergeActual (r6-provenance.mjs:36-42) picks, per exercise, the whole entry with the higher key [known count, set count, source rank, -reps, -rir, -load]; it does not merge fields. A manual entry with loads and reps (no RIR) and an agreeing device entry with reps and RIR (no loads) tie on known values (6 vs 6); the device entry wins on rank and every load of that exercise is dropped. This contradicts the function's own contract ('a known value is never replaced by an unknown one') and the cycle-2 test claim ('changes nothing, whatever it lists, omits').

newFindings.title: An event change that reaches this week discards the week's earlier same-week adaptations
newFindings.claimBroken: Headline invariant (same facts, same plan whatever the arrival order of same-week reviews); the cycle-2 QE-R7A-03 claim 'a rebuild that starts in the current week keeps what is not ahead and re-plans what is'
newFindings.mechanism: rebuild with fromWeek = w (r6-adaptation.mjs:458-460, new in cycle 2) re-projects the remaining days from stateTrace[w] and keeps only sessions that are not ahead. SYSTEMIC_FATIGUE, UNAVAILABLE_DAY, MISSED_SESSION moves and EVENT_WEEK_CONFLICT store their changes only in week w's session rows (stateTrace unchanged), so an event change afterwards silently undoes them. Before cycle 2 the event change never touched week w, so both orders composed.

newFindings.title: A new report's own provenance.mergedSourceIds / inputHashes register it under other event ids
newFindings.mechanism: normalizeObservations (r6-provenance.mjs:130) registers every accepted row under the keys of o.provenance.inputHashes and o.provenance.mergedSourceIds, including rows from review.observations (not carried); inputHashes from the input are also trusted (:89). QE-R7A-16's principle (only a carried row can be history) is not applied to merge provenance.

newFindings.whyNotBlocking: requires a client to send merge provenance on a new observation; same class and calibration as QE-R7A-16 (LOW)

newFindings.title: Three or more reports of one session: arrival order still decides
newFindings.mechanism: (i) the merged row keeps the first report's provenance.sourceQuality (r6-provenance.mjs:123), so later merges rank against it; (ii) agreement is checked against the merged row, not pairwise, so two contradicting reports merge when an intermediate one arrives first.
newFindings.whyNotBlocking: three reports of one session are rare; (i) reached no prescription in ten weeks; (ii) predates R7-A and both outcomes are conservative

observationsNotCounted: equipmentChange, fatigue, unavailableDay, eventWeekConflict and moveCandidates still use s.date > asOfLocal, while return, goal change and immutability use aheadOf: after a morning move to machines the same-day PM session keeps its barbell rows, and the equipment change's projected next-week state then differs from the reviewed one (4 entries in qe-recheck-P7.out.json 7b). The delta did not touch these lines; listed for R7-B.

SSCTR D55 (new in cycle 2): in the reviewed path, machine exercises first set up in step week 7 get returnInBlock and a regain cap (glute-bridge, lat-pulldown, machine-chest-press regainCap 3; reverse-lunge 2). Its dose semantics are the SSCTR's to rule.

Regression bookkeeping (regress-r7a.mjs norm drops entryWeek and inputHashes keys): every prescription and status is still compared, so ignoring them cannot hide a decision difference that the corpus exercises; it can only hide a latent state difference whose effect falls after a case ends (for example QE-R7A-15's flag at a case's last step). Not demonstrated in the corpus because regress-r7a.mjs writes under CoachingCore/ and was not run.

Week-level summary fields (plannedRunMinutes, plannedStrengthSets) of a week rebuilt from the current day are those of the full projection, not of the merged kept + fresh sessions; validation reads sessions only, so this is cosmetic.

verdict.reason: Eleven of the eighteen first-cycle findings are fixed (04, 06-11, 14-17), and the core mechanisms still hold (D53, single-branch phase dose, unknown repetitions, legacy hand-over, one count in projection and review). Five blockers are only partly fixed, each with a residual in the same mechanism and claim: 01 (an equipment change erases a next-week return, HIGH), 02 (SHORT-class first run back stays quality, MEDIUM), 03 (after a next-week return, a postponed race leaves two races, HIGH), 05 (the per-exercise merge drops a known load; over ten weeks four exercises are never established, MEDIUM) and 12 (a shortfall at a lighter load becomes the target, MEDIUM). The second cycle also introduced QE-R7A-19 (an event change that reaches this week erases that week's earlier fatigue reduction or unavailable-day reschedule, MEDIUM, blocking). STOP_WHEN ('no known HIGH structural failure of this phase stays open') is not met.

verdict.boundedCycle: Per TASK_CONTRACT.md this was the single narrow re-check; there is no further cycle. R7-A closes NOT_READY with the six blockers above named. Each is narrow and runtime-only, so it can be carried as a named entry into the next mission's scope without reopening R7-A.
